confidence_notes: I based the food and drink anchors on one web search of aggregated cost-of-living sites (nomad.watch, citycost.org, championtraveler.com and similar). The sources disagreed a lot. Inexpensive meals ranged from about $5 to $10, local beer from $1.50 to $5 and cappuccino from about $2.24 to $5.82. I picked tourist-town midpoints because Victoria Falls runs on US dollars and prices are aimed at tourists. The search returned no direct figures for cocktails or wine, so I set those from their usual price relationship to beer in tourist bars, with wine being mostly imported from South Africa. Those two anchors are less certain. Accommodation figures are my own estimates from general knowledge and were not checked against live listings. Accommodation in Victoria Falls is dear for the region, and July is peak dry season, so I pushed the hotel anchors up.
comparable_city_reasoning: I compared the town with Livingstone in Zambia and Kasane in Botswana. Like Victoria Falls, both are safari and falls gateway towns priced in US dollars for tourists. Prices in Victoria Falls are well above Zimbabwean towns such as Bulawayo and Gweru.
